  14 bright cyan     #72D8CA   teal+     — teal brightened (visibly lighter than #2CB9AA)
  15 bright white    #FFF8F0   crema     — full brightness
"""

import os
import sys
import plistlib
import struct

# ── Verify we're on macOS and PyObjC is available ────────────────────────────
if sys.platform != "darwin":
    sys.exit("ERROR: This script must be run on macOS.")

try:
    from Foundation import NSKeyedArchiver
    from AppKit import NSColor, NSFont
except ImportError:
    sys.exit(
        "ERROR: PyObjC is not available.\n"
        "This script requires the SYSTEM python3 at /usr/bin/python3.\n"
        "If /usr/bin/python3 reports this error, run:\n"
        "  xcode-select --install\n"
        "and then retry."
    )

# ── Color definitions ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Each tuple is (R, G, B) with components in 0.0–1.0 sRGB range.
# Converted from hex using component / 255.

def hex_to_rgb_floats(hex_str):
    """Convert '#RRGGBB' or 'RRGGBB' to (r, g, b) as 0.0–1.0 floats."""
    h = hex_str.lstrip('#')
    return tuple(int(h[i:i+2], 16) / 255.0 for i in (0, 2, 4))

PALETTE = {
    # Chrome
    "background":     "#241810",   # void
    "foreground":     "#FFF8F0",   # crema
    "cursor":         "#2CB9AA",   # teal
    "cursor_text":    "#241810",   # void (inverted on cursor block)
    "selection":      "#3B2A20",   # espresso (Terminal.app uses opaque selection bg)
    "bold_text":      "#FFF8F0",   # crema (bold = same color, different weight)

    # ANSI Normal 0–7
    "ansi_black":     "#2B1D14",   # obsidian
    "ansi_red":       "#FE8175",   # scarlet
    "ansi_green":     "#79B56C",   # sage
    "ansi_yellow":    "#E9922E",   # amber
    "ansi_blue":      "#6AACE2",   # slate
    "ansi_magenta":   "#D28DE2",   # mauve
    "ansi_cyan":      "#2CB9AA",   # teal
    "ansi_white":     "#E9DCCF",   # bone

    # ANSI Bright 8–15
    "ansi_bright_black":   "#BCA18A",  # crater-deep
    "ansi_bright_red":     "#FF9286",  # scarlet lightened
    "ansi_bright_green":   "#98D083",  # sage lightened
    "ansi_bright_yellow":  "#D0A200",  # gold
    "ansi_bright_blue":    "#68C7F4",  # slate lightened
    "ansi_bright_magenta": "#E792DF",  # mauve lightened
    "ansi_bright_cyan":    "#72D8CA",  # teal brightened (lighter than #2CB9AA)
    "ansi_bright_white":   "#FFF8F0",  # crema
}

# Terminal.app plist key names for each palette entry
PLIST_KEYS = {
    "background":          "BackgroundColor",
    "foreground":          "TextColor",
    "cursor":              "CursorColor",
    "cursor_text":         "CursorTextColor",
    "selection":           "SelectionColor",
    "bold_text":           "TextBoldColor",

    "ansi_black":          "ANSIBlackColor",
    "ansi_red":            "ANSIRedColor",
    "ansi_green":          "ANSIGreenColor",
    "ansi_yellow":         "ANSIYellowColor",
    "ansi_blue":           "ANSIBlueColor",
    "ansi_magenta":        "ANSIMagentaColor",
    "ansi_cyan":           "ANSICyanColor",
    "ansi_white":          "ANSIWhiteColor",

    "ansi_bright_black":   "ANSIBrightBlackColor",
    "ansi_bright_red":     "ANSIBrightRedColor",
    "ansi_bright_green":   "ANSIBrightGreenColor",
    "ansi_bright_yellow":  "ANSIBrightYellowColor",
    "ansi_bright_blue":    "ANSIBrightBlueColor",
    "ansi_bright_magenta": "ANSIBrightMagentaColor",
    "ansi_bright_cyan":    "ANSIBrightCyanColor",
    "ansi_bright_white":   "ANSIBrightWhiteColor",
}


def archive_nsobject(value):
    """Archive an AppKit object and surface any NSError returned by PyObjC."""
    result = NSKeyedArchiver.archivedDataWithRootObject_requiringSecureCoding_error_(
        value, False, None
    )
    if isinstance(result, tuple):
        data, error = result
    else:
        data, error = result, None
    if data is None:
        raise RuntimeError(f"NSKeyedArchiver failed: {error}")
    return bytes(data)


def color_to_nsdata(hex_color):
    """
    Convert a hex color string to NSData containing an NSKeyedArchiver-encoded
    NSColor object. This is the exact format Terminal.app expects in its plist.

    NSColor objects are serialized via NSKeyedArchiver because Terminal.app
    needs to round-trip them through Core Data. Plain hex is not accepted.
    """
    r, g, b = hex_to_rgb_floats(hex_color)
    # Create an sRGB NSColor with alpha = 1.0
    color = NSColor.colorWithSRGBRed_green_blue_alpha_(r, g, b, 1.0)
    return archive_nsobject(color)


def make_font_nsdata(family="Menlo", size=13.0):
    """
    Create NSKeyedArchiver-encoded NSFont data for the terminal font.
    Menlo 13pt is Terminal.app's default monospace font.
    """
    font = NSFont.fontWithName_size_(family, size)
    if font is None:
        # Fallback: try Monaco if Menlo somehow unavailable
        font = NSFont.fontWithName_size_("Monaco", size)
    if font is None:
        print(f"WARNING: Could not find font '{family}', skipping Font key.")
        return None
    return archive_nsobject(font)


def build_profile():
    """
    Build the complete Terminal.app profile plist dictionary.

    ProfileCurrentVersion 2.07 is the format used by Terminal on macOS 12+.
    The 'type' key must be exactly "Window Settings" — Terminal.app ignores
    profiles without this key.
    """
    profile = {
        # ── Profile metadata ─────────────────────────────────────────────
        "name":                   "Dark Roast House Blend",
        "type":                   "Window Settings",
        "ProfileCurrentVersion":  2.07,

        # ── Window size ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
        "columnCount":            220,
        "rowCount":               50,

        # ── Cursor style ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
        # 0 = block, 1 = underline, 2 = vertical bar
        "CursorType":             0,
        "CursorBlink":            True,

        # ── Text settings ────────────────────────────────────────────────
        "UseBoldFonts":           True,
        "UseBlinkingText":        False,
        "DisableANSIColor":       False,
        # Terminal.app uses "bright colors for bold text" by default —
        # we disable this so bold uses TextBoldColor (#FFF8F0) not the
        # bright ANSI variant.
        "UseBrightBold":          False,

        # ── Background opacity ───────────────────────────────────────────
        # 1.0 = fully opaque — required for warm-dark void to work correctly.
        # Transparency would blend void with desktop wallpaper.
        "BackgroundAlphaInactive": 1.0,
        "BackgroundBlur":          0.0,

        # ── Scrollback ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
        "ScrollbackLines":        10000,
        "ScrollbackUnlimited":    False,

        # ── Bell ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
        "Bell":                   False,
        "VisualBell":             False,
    }

    # ── Colors ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    for palette_key, plist_key in PLIST_KEYS.items():
        hex_color = PALETTE[palette_key]
        profile[plist_key] = color_to_nsdata(hex_color)

    # ── Font ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    font_data = make_font_nsdata("Menlo", 13.0)
    if font_data:
        profile["Font"] = font_data

    return profile


def main():
    output_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
    output_path = os.path.join(output_dir, "Dark Roast House Blend.terminal")

    print("Dark Roast: House Blend — Terminal.app Profile Generator")
    print("=" * 60)
    print(f"Output: {output_path}")
    print()

    profile = build_profile()

    # Write as binary plist (required — Terminal.app rejects XML plist format
    # for color profiles because NSData values must be binary-encoded)
    with open(output_path, "wb") as f:
        plistlib.dump(profile, f, fmt=plistlib.FMT_XML)

    print(f"SUCCESS: Written to '{os.path.basename(output_path)}'")
    print()
    print("NEXT STEPS:")
    print("  1. Double-click the .terminal file in Finder, OR run:")
    print(f"       open \"{output_path}\"")
    print("  2. Terminal.app will import the profile automatically.")
    print("  3. To set as default: Terminal → Settings → Profiles →")
    print("     select 'Dark Roast House Blend' → click 'Default'.")
    print()
    print("ANSI PALETTE LOADED:")
    ansi_names = [
        ("0 black (obsidian)",        "ansi_black"),
        ("1 red (scarlet)",           "ansi_red"),
        ("2 green (sage)",            "ansi_green"),
        ("3 yellow (amber)",          "ansi_yellow"),
        ("4 blue (slate)",            "ansi_blue"),
        ("5 magenta (mauve)",         "ansi_magenta"),
        ("6 cyan (teal)",             "ansi_cyan"),
        ("7 white (bone)",            "ansi_white"),
        ("8 br.black (crater-deep)",  "ansi_bright_black"),
        ("9 br.red",                  "ansi_bright_red"),
        ("10 br.green",               "ansi_bright_green"),
        ("11 br.yellow (gold)",       "ansi_bright_yellow"),
        ("12 br.blue",                "ansi_bright_blue"),
        ("13 br.magenta",             "ansi_bright_magenta"),
        ("14 br.cyan (teal+)",        "ansi_bright_cyan"),
        ("15 br.white (crema)",       "ansi_bright_white"),
    ]
    for label, key in ansi_names:
        print(f"  {label:<28}  {PALETTE[key]}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

WHAT THIS SCRIPT DOES

------------
- macOS (any modern version — 10.15 Catalina or later recommended)

  PyObjC is only available on the system installation:
    /usr/bin/python3 generate-nitro-profile.py

  DO NOT use:
    python3 generate-nitro-profile.py   (if python3 points to Homebrew)
    ~/.pyenv/shims/python3 ...

INSTALL
-------
1. Run this script:
     /usr/bin/python3 generate-nitro-profile.py

2. A file named "Dark Roast Nitro.terminal" will be created in the
   current directory (same folder as this script).

3. Double-click "Dark Roast Nitro.terminal" in Finder, OR:
     open "Dark Roast Nitro.terminal"

   Terminal.app will import the profile automatically and prompt you to
   set it as default if desired.

4. To activate permanently:
   Terminal.app → Settings → Profiles → select "Dark Roast Nitro"
   → click "Default" button at the bottom of the list

ALTERNATIVE: Apply via defaults write (no file needed)

import os
import sys
import plistlib
import struct

# ── Verify we're on macOS and PyObjC is available ────────────────────────────
if sys.platform != "darwin":
    sys.exit("ERROR: This script must be run on macOS.")

try:
    from Foundation import NSColor, NSKeyedArchiver, NSData
    from AppKit import NSFont
except ImportError:
    sys.exit(
        "ERROR: PyObjC is not available.\n"
        "This script requires the SYSTEM python3 at /usr/bin/python3.\n"
        "If /usr/bin/python3 reports this error, run:\n"
        "  xcode-select --install\n"
        "and then retry."
    )

# ── Color definitions ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Each tuple is (R, G, B) with components in 0.0–1.0 sRGB range.
# Converted from hex using component / 255.

def hex_to_rgb_floats(hex_str):
    """Convert '#RRGGBB' or 'RRGGBB' to (r, g, b) as 0.0–1.0 floats."""
    h = hex_str.lstrip('#')
    return tuple(int(h[i:i+2], 16) / 255.0 for i in (0, 2, 4))

PALETTE = {
    # Chrome
    "background":     "#120C06",   # void
    "foreground":     "#FFF7EE",   # crema
    "cursor":         "#4CC4B4",   # teal
    "cursor_text":    "#120C06",   # void (inverted on cursor block)
    "selection":      "#2A1C13",   # espresso (Terminal.app uses opaque selection bg)
    "bold_text":      "#FFF7EE",   # crema (bold = same color, different weight)

    # ANSI Normal 0–7
    "ansi_black":     "#160E08",   # obsidian
    "ansi_red":       "#C44C4C",   # scarlet
    "ansi_green":     "#8AAC6B",   # sage
    "ansi_yellow":    "#E69A4C",   # amber
    "ansi_blue":      "#6E8FAD",   # slate
    "ansi_magenta":   "#AD7FA8",   # mauve
    "ansi_cyan":      "#4CC4B4",   # teal
    "ansi_white":     "#EBE1D7",   # bone

    # ANSI Bright 8–15
    "ansi_bright_black":   "#3C2A21",  # crater-deep
    "ansi_bright_red":     "#D46868",  # scarlet lightened
    "ansi_bright_green":   "#A3C484",  # sage lightened
    "ansi_bright_yellow":  "#DAA520",  # gold
    "ansi_bright_blue":    "#8AABC4",  # slate lightened
    "ansi_bright_magenta": "#C49BC0",  # mauve lightened
    "ansi_bright_cyan":    "#6DD4C8",  # teal brightened (lighter than #4CC4B4)
    "ansi_bright_white":   "#FFF7EE",  # crema
}

# Terminal.app plist key names for each palette entry
PLIST_KEYS = {
    "background":          "BackgroundColor",
    "foreground":          "TextColor",
    "cursor":              "CursorColor",
    "cursor_text":         "CursorTextColor",
    "selection":           "SelectionColor",
    "bold_text":           "TextBoldColor",

    "ansi_black":          "ANSIBlackColor",
    "ansi_red":            "ANSIRedColor",
    "ansi_green":          "ANSIGreenColor",
    "ansi_yellow":         "ANSIYellowColor",
    "ansi_blue":           "ANSIBlueColor",
    "ansi_magenta":        "ANSIMagentaColor",
    "ansi_cyan":           "ANSICyanColor",
    "ansi_white":          "ANSIWhiteColor",

    "ansi_bright_black":   "ANSIBrightBlackColor",
    "ansi_bright_red":     "ANSIBrightRedColor",
    "ansi_bright_green":   "ANSIBrightGreenColor",
    "ansi_bright_yellow":  "ANSIBrightYellowColor",
    "ansi_bright_blue":    "ANSIBrightBlueColor",
    "ansi_bright_magenta": "ANSIBrightMagentaColor",
    "ansi_bright_cyan":    "ANSIBrightCyanColor",
    "ansi_bright_white":   "ANSIBrightWhiteColor",
}


def color_to_nsdata(hex_color):
    """
    Convert a hex color string to NSData containing an NSKeyedArchiver-encoded
    NSColor object. This is the exact format Terminal.app expects in its plist.

    NSColor objects are serialized via NSKeyedArchiver because Terminal.app
    needs to round-trip them through Core Data. Plain hex is not accepted.
    """
    r, g, b = hex_to_rgb_floats(hex_color)
    # Create an sRGB NSColor with alpha = 1.0
    color = NSColor.colorWithSRGBRed_green_blue_alpha_(r, g, b, 1.0)
    # Archive it using NSKeyedArchiver
    data = NSKeyedArchiver.archivedDataWithRootObject_requiringSecureCoding_error_(
        color, False, None
    )
    # data is NSData; convert to Python bytes for plistlib
    return bytes(data)


def make_font_nsdata(family="Menlo", size=13.0):
    """
    Create NSKeyedArchiver-encoded NSFont data for the terminal font.
    Menlo 13pt is Terminal.app's default monospace font.
    """
    font = NSFont.fontWithName_size_(family, size)
    if font is None:
        # Fallback: try Monaco if Menlo somehow unavailable
        font = NSFont.fontWithName_size_("Monaco", size)
    if font is None:
        print(f"WARNING: Could not find font '{family}', skipping Font key.")
        return None
    data = NSKeyedArchiver.archivedDataWithRootObject_requiringSecureCoding_error_(
        font, False, None
    )
    return bytes(data)


def build_profile():
    """
    Build the complete Terminal.app profile plist dictionary.

    ProfileCurrentVersion 2.07 is the format used by Terminal on macOS 12+.
    The 'type' key must be exactly "Window Settings" — Terminal.app ignores
    profiles without this key.
    """
    profile = {
        # ── Profile metadata ─────────────────────────────────────────────
        "name":                   "Dark Roast Black Label",
        "type":                   "Window Settings",
        "ProfileCurrentVersion":  2.07,

        # ── Window size ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
        "columnCount":            220,
        "rowCount":               50,

        # ── Cursor style ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
        # 0 = block, 1 = underline, 2 = vertical bar
        "CursorType":             0,
        "CursorBlink":            True,

        # ── Text settings ────────────────────────────────────────────────
        "UseBoldFonts":           True,
        "UseBlinkingText":        False,
        "DisableANSIColor":       False,
        # Terminal.app uses "bright colors for bold text" by default —
        # we disable this so bold uses TextBoldColor (#FFF7EE) not the
        # bright ANSI variant.
        "UseBrightBold":          False,

        # ── Background opacity ───────────────────────────────────────────
        # 1.0 = fully opaque — required for OLED-black void to work correctly.
        # Transparency would blend void with desktop wallpaper.
        "BackgroundAlphaInactive": 1.0,
        "BackgroundBlur":          0.0,

        # ── Scrollback ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
        "ScrollbackLines":        10000,
        "ScrollbackUnlimited":    False,

        # ── Bell ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
        "Bell":                   False,
        "VisualBell":             False,
    }

    # ── Colors ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    for palette_key, plist_key in PLIST_KEYS.items():
        hex_color = PALETTE[palette_key]
        profile[plist_key] = color_to_nsdata(hex_color)

    # ── Font ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    font_data = make_font_nsdata("Menlo", 13.0)
    if font_data:
        profile["Font"] = font_data

    return profile


def main():
    output_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
    output_path = os.path.join(output_dir, "Dark Roast Black Label.terminal")

    print("Dark Roast: Black Label — Terminal.app Profile Generator")
    print("=" * 60)
    print(f"Output: {output_path}")
    print()

    profile = build_profile()

    # Write as binary plist (required — Terminal.app rejects XML plist format
    # for color profiles because NSData values must be binary-encoded)
    with open(output_path, "wb") as f:
        plistlib.dump(profile, f, fmt=plistlib.FMT_XML)

    print(f"SUCCESS: Written to '{os.path.basename(output_path)}'")
    print()
    print("NEXT STEPS:")
    print("  1. Double-click the .terminal file in Finder, OR run:")
    print(f"       open \"{output_path}\"")
    print("  2. Terminal.app will import the profile automatically.")
    print("  3. To set as default: Terminal → Settings → Profiles →")
    print("     select 'Dark Roast Black Label' → click 'Default'.")
    print()
    print("ANSI PALETTE LOADED:")
    ansi_names = [
        ("0 black (obsidian)",        "ansi_black"),
        ("1 red (scarlet)",           "ansi_red"),
        ("2 green (sage)",            "ansi_green"),
        ("3 yellow (amber)",          "ansi_yellow"),
        ("4 blue (slate)",            "ansi_blue"),
        ("5 magenta (mauve)",         "ansi_magenta"),
        ("6 cyan (teal)",             "ansi_cyan"),
        ("7 white (bone)",            "ansi_white"),
        ("8 br.black (crater-deep)",  "ansi_bright_black"),
        ("9 br.red",                  "ansi_bright_red"),
        ("10 br.green",               "ansi_bright_green"),
        ("11 br.yellow (gold)",       "ansi_bright_yellow"),
        ("12 br.blue",                "ansi_bright_blue"),
        ("13 br.magenta",             "ansi_bright_magenta"),
        ("14 br.cyan (teal+)",        "ansi_bright_cyan"),
        ("15 br.white (crema)",       "ansi_bright_white"),
    ]
    for label, key in ansi_names:
        print(f"  {label:<28}  {PALETTE[key]}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""
Dark Roast: Velvet Noir — Terminal.app Profile Generator
Version: 5.1.0 Companion

WHAT THIS SCRIPT DOES
---------------------
Generates "Dark Roast Velvet Noir.terminal" — an Apple Terminal.app color
profile (.terminal file) with the full Dark Roast ANSI-16 palette.

Terminal.app stores colors as NSKeyedArchiver-serialized NSColor objects
embedded in a binary plist, which is then base64-encoded. This makes the
format impossible to write by hand (unlike iTerm2's .itermcolors). This
script uses PyObjC (the Python–Objective-C bridge that ships with every
macOS system Python installation) to produce the correct binary encoding.

REQUIREMENTS
------------
- macOS (any modern version — 10.15 Catalina or later recommended)
- Python 3 — use the SYSTEM python3, not a venv or Homebrew python, because
  PyObjC is only available on the system installation:
    /usr/bin/python3 generate-velvet-noir-profile.py

  DO NOT use:
    python3 generate-velvet-noir-profile.py   (if python3 points to Homebrew)
    ~/.pyenv/shims/python3 ...

INSTALL
-------
1. Run this script:
     /usr/bin/python3 generate-velvet-noir-profile.py

2. A file named "Dark Roast Velvet Noir.terminal" will be created in the
   current directory (same folder as this script).

def archive_nsobject(value):
    """Archive an AppKit object and surface any NSError returned by PyObjC."""
    result = NSKeyedArchiver.archivedDataWithRootObject_requiringSecureCoding_error_(
        value, False, None
    )
    if isinstance(result, tuple):
        data, error = result
    else:
        data, error = result, None
    if data is None:
        raise RuntimeError(f"NSKeyedArchiver failed: {error}")
    return bytes(data)


def color_to_nsdata(hex_color):
    """
    Convert a hex color string to NSData containing an NSKeyedArchiver-encoded
    NSColor object. This is the exact format Terminal.app expects in its plist.

    NSColor objects are serialized via NSKeyedArchiver because Terminal.app
    needs to round-trip them through Core Data. Plain hex is not accepted.

    color = NSColor.colorWithSRGBRed_green_blue_alpha_(r, g, b, 1.0)
    return archive_nsobject(color)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# AUTO-GENERATED by scripts/build-variants.js — DO NOT EDIT.
"""
Dark Roast: Velvet — Terminal.app Profile Generator
Version: 5.1.0 Companion

WHAT THIS SCRIPT DOES
---------------------
Generates "Dark Roast Velvet.terminal" — an Apple Terminal.app color
profile (.terminal file) with the full Dark Roast ANSI-16 palette.

Terminal.app stores colors as NSKeyedArchiver-serialized NSColor objects
embedded in a binary plist, which is then base64-encoded. This makes the
format impossible to write by hand (unlike iTerm2's .itermcolors). This
script uses PyObjC (the Python–Objective-C bridge that ships with every
macOS system Python installation) to produce the correct binary encoding.

REQUIREMENTS
------------
- macOS (any modern version — 10.15 Catalina or later recommended)
- Python 3 — use the SYSTEM python3, not a venv or Homebrew python, because
  PyObjC is only available on the system installation:
    /usr/bin/python3 generate-velvet-profile.py

  DO NOT use:
    python3 generate-velvet-profile.py   (if python3 points to Homebrew)
    ~/.pyenv/shims/python3 ...

INSTALL
-------
1. Run this script:
     /usr/bin/python3 generate-velvet-profile.py

2. A file named "Dark Roast Velvet.terminal" will be created in the
   current directory (same folder as this script).

3. Double-click "Dark Roast Velvet.terminal" in Finder, OR:
     open "Dark Roast Velvet.terminal"

   Terminal.app will import the profile automatically and prompt you to
   set it as default if desired.

4. To activate permanently:
   Terminal.app → Settings → Profiles → select "Dark Roast Velvet"
   → click "Default" button at the bottom of the list

ALTERNATIVE: Apply via defaults write (no file needed)
------------------------------------------------------
If you prefer to apply the profile directly without generating a file, see
the companion script install.sh in this same directory.

FULL COLOR REFERENCE
--------------------
Chrome:
  background    #190605   void      — warm-dark deepest layer
  foreground    #F7EADE   crema     — primary text (16.62:1 contrast on void)
  cursor        #42B3A8   teal      — kinetic cursor, matches editor caret
  cursor text   #190605   void      — text color inside cursor block
  selection     #3B1817   espresso  — warm polished surface (v4: was `grain`)
  bold          #F7EADE   crema     — same as foreground (bold = same weight)

ANSI Normal (indices 0–7):
  0  black       #240A09   obsidian  — dark floor (not as deep as void)
  1  red         #D4494E   scarlet   — error / critical
  2  green       #60A659   sage      — warm fern (terminal extension)
  3  yellow      #E18826   amber     — warning / accent
  4  blue        #608BB7   slate     — dusty steel (terminal extension)
  5  magenta     #BC60AD   mauve     — dried lavender (terminal extension)
  6  cyan        #42B3A8   teal      — live data flow
  7  white       #E4D1C2   bone      — reduced-contrast light text

ANSI Bright (indices 8–15):
  8  bright black    #AC8981   crater-deep — comment gray (v4: was `crater`)
  9  bright red      #ED6667   scarlet+  — scarlet companion-bright
  10 bright green    #7EBE77   sage+     — sage companion-bright
  11 bright yellow   #E4AE28   gold      — success / stable severity
  12 bright blue     #77A3D0   slate+    — slate companion-bright
  13 bright magenta  #D47AC4   mauve+    — mauve companion-bright
  14 bright cyan     #63CDC1   teal+     — teal brightened (visibly lighter than #42B3A8)
  15 bright white    #F7EADE   crema     — full brightness
"""

import os
import sys
import plistlib
import struct

# ── Verify we're on macOS and PyObjC is available ────────────────────────────
if sys.platform != "darwin":
    sys.exit("ERROR: This script must be run on macOS.")

try:
    from Foundation import NSKeyedArchiver
    from AppKit import NSColor, NSFont
except ImportError:
    sys.exit(
        "ERROR: PyObjC is not available.\n"
        "This script requires the SYSTEM python3 at /usr/bin/python3.\n"
        "If /usr/bin/python3 reports this error, run:\n"
        "  xcode-select --install\n"
        "and then retry."
    )

# ── Color definitions ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Each tuple is (R, G, B) with components in 0.0–1.0 sRGB range.
# Converted from hex using component / 255.

def hex_to_rgb_floats(hex_str):
    """Convert '#RRGGBB' or 'RRGGBB' to (r, g, b) as 0.0–1.0 floats."""
    h = hex_str.lstrip('#')
    return tuple(int(h[i:i+2], 16) / 255.0 for i in (0, 2, 4))

PALETTE = {
    # Chrome
    "background":     "#190605",   # void
    "foreground":     "#F7EADE",   # crema
    "cursor":         "#42B3A8",   # teal
    "cursor_text":    "#190605",   # void (inverted on cursor block)
    "selection":      "#3B1817",   # espresso (Terminal.app uses opaque selection bg)
    "bold_text":      "#F7EADE",   # crema (bold = same color, different weight)

    # ANSI Normal 0–7
    "ansi_black":     "#240A09",   # obsidian
    "ansi_red":       "#D4494E",   # scarlet
    "ansi_green":     "#60A659",   # sage
    "ansi_yellow":    "#E18826",   # amber
    "ansi_blue":      "#608BB7",   # slate
    "ansi_magenta":   "#BC60AD",   # mauve
    "ansi_cyan":      "#42B3A8",   # teal
    "ansi_white":     "#E4D1C2",   # bone

    # ANSI Bright 8–15
    "ansi_bright_black":   "#AC8981",  # crater-deep
    "ansi_bright_red":     "#ED6667",  # scarlet lightened
    "ansi_bright_green":   "#7EBE77",  # sage lightened
    "ansi_bright_yellow":  "#E4AE28",  # gold
    "ansi_bright_blue":    "#77A3D0",  # slate lightened
    "ansi_bright_magenta": "#D47AC4",  # mauve lightened
    "ansi_bright_cyan":    "#63CDC1",  # teal brightened (lighter than #42B3A8)
    "ansi_bright_white":   "#F7EADE",  # crema
}

# Terminal.app plist key names for each palette entry
PLIST_KEYS = {
    "background":          "BackgroundColor",
    "foreground":          "TextColor",
    "cursor":              "CursorColor",
    "cursor_text":         "CursorTextColor",
    "selection":           "SelectionColor",
    "bold_text":           "TextBoldColor",

    "ansi_black":          "ANSIBlackColor",
    "ansi_red":            "ANSIRedColor",
    "ansi_green":          "ANSIGreenColor",
    "ansi_yellow":         "ANSIYellowColor",
    "ansi_blue":           "ANSIBlueColor",
    "ansi_magenta":        "ANSIMagentaColor",
    "ansi_cyan":           "ANSICyanColor",
    "ansi_white":          "ANSIWhiteColor",

    "ansi_bright_black":   "ANSIBrightBlackColor",
    "ansi_bright_red":     "ANSIBrightRedColor",
    "ansi_bright_green":   "ANSIBrightGreenColor",
    "ansi_bright_yellow":  "ANSIBrightYellowColor",
    "ansi_bright_blue":    "ANSIBrightBlueColor",
    "ansi_bright_magenta": "ANSIBrightMagentaColor",
    "ansi_bright_cyan":    "ANSIBrightCyanColor",
    "ansi_bright_white":   "ANSIBrightWhiteColor",
}


def archive_nsobject(value):
    """Archive an AppKit object and surface any NSError returned by PyObjC."""
    result = NSKeyedArchiver.archivedDataWithRootObject_requiringSecureCoding_error_(
        value, False, None
    )
    if isinstance(result, tuple):
        data, error = result
    else:
        data, error = result, None
    if data is None:
        raise RuntimeError(f"NSKeyedArchiver failed: {error}")
    return bytes(data)


def color_to_nsdata(hex_color):
    """
    Convert a hex color string to NSData containing an NSKeyedArchiver-encoded
    NSColor object. This is the exact format Terminal.app expects in its plist.

    NSColor objects are serialized via NSKeyedArchiver because Terminal.app
    needs to round-trip them through Core Data. Plain hex is not accepted.
    """
    r, g, b = hex_to_rgb_floats(hex_color)
    # Create an sRGB NSColor with alpha = 1.0
    color = NSColor.colorWithSRGBRed_green_blue_alpha_(r, g, b, 1.0)
    return archive_nsobject(color)


def make_font_nsdata(family="Menlo", size=13.0):
    """
    Create NSKeyedArchiver-encoded NSFont data for the terminal font.
    Menlo 13pt is Terminal.app's default monospace font.
    """
    font = NSFont.fontWithName_size_(family, size)
    if font is None:
        # Fallback: try Monaco if Menlo somehow unavailable
        font = NSFont.fontWithName_size_("Monaco", size)
    if font is None:
        print(f"WARNING: Could not find font '{family}', skipping Font key.")
        return None
    return archive_nsobject(font)


def build_profile():
    """
    Build the complete Terminal.app profile plist dictionary.

    ProfileCurrentVersion 2.07 is the format used by Terminal on macOS 12+.
    The 'type' key must be exactly "Window Settings" — Terminal.app ignores
    profiles without this key.
    """
    profile = {
        # ── Profile metadata ─────────────────────────────────────────────
        "name":                   "Dark Roast Velvet",
        "type":                   "Window Settings",
        "ProfileCurrentVersion":  2.07,

        # ── Window size ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
        "columnCount":            220,
        "rowCount":               50,

        # ── Cursor style ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
        # 0 = block, 1 = underline, 2 = vertical bar
        "CursorType":             0,
        "CursorBlink":            True,

        # ── Text settings ────────────────────────────────────────────────
        "UseBoldFonts":           True,
        "UseBlinkingText":        False,
        "DisableANSIColor":       False,
        # Terminal.app uses "bright colors for bold text" by default —
        # we disable this so bold uses TextBoldColor (#F7EADE) not the
        # bright ANSI variant.
        "UseBrightBold":          False,

        # ── Background opacity ───────────────────────────────────────────
        # 1.0 = fully opaque — required for warm-dark void to work correctly.
        # Transparency would blend void with desktop wallpaper.
        "BackgroundAlphaInactive": 1.0,
        "BackgroundBlur":          0.0,

        # ── Scrollback ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
        "ScrollbackLines":        10000,
        "ScrollbackUnlimited":    False,

        # ── Bell ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
        "Bell":                   False,
        "VisualBell":             False,
    }

    # ── Colors ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    for palette_key, plist_key in PLIST_KEYS.items():
        hex_color = PALETTE[palette_key]
        profile[plist_key] = color_to_nsdata(hex_color)

    # ── Font ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    font_data = make_font_nsdata("Menlo", 13.0)
    if font_data:
        profile["Font"] = font_data

    return profile


def main():
    output_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
    output_path = os.path.join(output_dir, "Dark Roast Velvet.terminal")

    print("Dark Roast: Velvet — Terminal.app Profile Generator")
    print("=" * 60)
    print(f"Output: {output_path}")
    print()

    profile = build_profile()

    # Write as binary plist (required — Terminal.app rejects XML plist format
    # for color profiles because NSData values must be binary-encoded)
    with open(output_path, "wb") as f:
        plistlib.dump(profile, f, fmt=plistlib.FMT_XML)

    print(f"SUCCESS: Written to '{os.path.basename(output_path)}'")
    print()
    print("NEXT STEPS:")
    print("  1. Double-click the .terminal file in Finder, OR run:")
    print(f"       open \"{output_path}\"")
    print("  2. Terminal.app will import the profile automatically.")
    print("  3. To set as default: Terminal → Settings → Profiles →")
    print("     select 'Dark Roast Velvet' → click 'Default'.")
    print()
    print("ANSI PALETTE LOADED:")
    ansi_names = [
        ("0 black (obsidian)",        "ansi_black"),
        ("1 red (scarlet)",           "ansi_red"),
        ("2 green (sage)",            "ansi_green"),
        ("3 yellow (amber)",          "ansi_yellow"),
        ("4 blue (slate)",            "ansi_blue"),
        ("5 magenta (mauve)",         "ansi_magenta"),
        ("6 cyan (teal)",             "ansi_cyan"),
        ("7 white (bone)",            "ansi_white"),
        ("8 br.black (crater-deep)",  "ansi_bright_black"),
        ("9 br.red",                  "ansi_bright_red"),
        ("10 br.green",               "ansi_bright_green"),
        ("11 br.yellow (gold)",       "ansi_bright_yellow"),
        ("12 br.blue",                "ansi_bright_blue"),
        ("13 br.magenta",             "ansi_bright_magenta"),
        ("14 br.cyan (teal+)",        "ansi_bright_cyan"),
        ("15 br.white (crema)",       "ansi_bright_white"),
    ]
    for label, key in ansi_names:
        print(f"  {label:<28}  {PALETTE[key]}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    <!-- ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
         §28  INVALID & DEPRECATED
         ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
         Scarlet (#f86572) is the ONLY correct use for error-state code.
         The canonical spec reserves scarlet for actual errors — which is
         why keywords were deliberately moved to mauve.
         Deprecated tokens use amber-hot + strikethrough: warning, not error.

    <!-- ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
         §20  MARKDOWN
         ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
         Markdown is a writing format as much as a code format. The color
         scheme treats it as structured content: headings are landmarks
         (amber bold), bold/italic are emphasis (gold), code is data (sage),
         links are navigable (teal underline), blockquotes are quotes (mocha).

  │  DESIGN PHILOSOPHY                                                      │
  │                                                                         │
  │  This theme maps the somaNotes Dark Roast design system (dark-roast-    │

  │  is CONSISTENT across all editors (Textastic, Sublime Text, VS Code     │

  │                                                                         │
  │  OLED-AWARE: warm cocoa surfaces preserve depth and edge definition.  │
  │  They do not rely on absolute black as the only source of contrast.   │
  │                                                                         │
  │                                                                         │
  │  LONG-SESSION PALETTE: warm and cool roles make syntax scannable.     │
  │  Mauve marks structure, sage marks data, and teal marks user actions. │
  │  The warm canvas avoids the glare of a cool high-contrast background. │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  ┌─────────────────────┬───────────┬──────────┬──────────────────────────────┐

===== FILE: dark-roast-theme/platforms/vscode/themes/dark-roast-color-theme.json =====
{
  // Dark Roast: Black Label — VS Code / Cursor Color Theme
  // Version: 4.0.0
  //
  // Design system: surface scale (void, obsidian, dark-cacao, espresso, espresso-hover,
  // roasted-bean, crater), foregrounds (crema, warm-white, bone, mocha), geological
  // (crater-deep, asparagus, rustic, rose), action (amber, amber-hot, amber-muted, gold,
  // brass, scarlet, burnt-sienna, teal), and syntax extras (sage, slate, mauve).
  //
  // v4 migration (hex unchanged; only names changed):
  //   grain → espresso (#2A1C13), grain-hover → espresso-hover (#382818)
  //   crater (old) → crater-deep (#3C2A21), crater-lt → crater (#4D3B31)
  //
  // Philosophy: 12-hour-shift optimization. Every color chosen for minimal eye fatigue
  // over extended sessions. Warm-toned backgrounds (void #120C06) keep OLED pixels
  // active at 1.6ms wake, avoiding purple smear of pure black. Cool/warm contrast
  // between functions (slate) and types (gold) makes code scannable without conscious effort.
  //
  // Palette quick reference:
  //   void         #120C06   deepest background (L0: editor)
  //   obsidian     #1E140E   elevated surface (L1: sidebar, terminal, agent panel)
  //   espresso     #2A1C13   window frame (L2: title bar, activity bar, status bar, tab strip)
  //   espresso-hov #382818   hover / active widgets (L3)
  //   crema        #FFF7EE   primary text
  //   bone         #EBE1D7   reduced-contrast text
  //   mocha        #8B7355   secondary / captions
  //   asparagus    #465945   tertiary metadata
  //   crater-deep  #3C2A21   borders (was `crater` in v3 comments below)
  //   crater       #4D3B31   strong borders / inactive text (was `crater-lt`)
  //   amber        #E69A4C   primary accent / decorators
  //   amber-hot    #D2691E   numbers / constants / regex
  //   gold         #DAA520   types / success
  //   scarlet      #C44C4C   errors / HTML tags / escape chars
  //   burnt-sienna #C75B39   terminal red (new in v4)
  //   teal         #4CC4B4   operators / live data / links
  //   sage         #8AAC6B   strings / diff-added
  //   slate        #6E8FAD   functions / JSON keys / CSS props
  //   mauve        #AD7FA8   keywords / self/this
  //
  // NOTE: Inline comments below still use v3 names (grain/crater/crater-lt) as role
  // descriptors — they're cosmetic. Hex values are authoritative.

  "name": "Dark Roast: Black Label",
  "type": "dark",
  "semanticHighlighting": true,

  // ==========================================================================
  // UI CHROME COLORS
  // Every VS Code surface, widget, and decoration.
  // ==========================================================================
  "colors": {

    // ── Global foreground / focus ──────────────────────────────────────────
    // focusBorder: the ring drawn around the focused element (buttons, inputs, etc.)
    "focusBorder": "#4CC4B4",
    "foreground": "#FFF7EE",
    "descriptionForeground": "#8B7355",
    "disabledForeground": "#465945",
    "errorForeground": "#C44C4C",
    "icon.foreground": "#8B7355",
    // selection uses amber at 27% opacity — warm, not visually jarring
    "selection.background": "#E69A4C44",
    "widget.shadow": "#0A060355",
    "widget.border": "#3C2A21",

    // ── Text colors (used in welcome pages, settings, etc.) ───────────────
    "textLink.foreground": "#4CC4B4",
    "textLink.activeForeground": "#6ED8CA",
    "textBlockQuote.background": "#160E08",
    "textBlockQuote.border": "#E69A4C",
    "textCodeBlock.background": "#2A1C13",
    "textPreformat.foreground": "#8AAC6B",
    "textSeparator.foreground": "#3C2A21",

    // ── Editor core ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    // Background is void (#120C06) — the deepest OLED-safe warm black.
    "editor.background": "#120C06",
    "editor.foreground": "#FFF7EE",
    // Teal cursor — kinetic, impossible to miss, aligns with "live data" semantics.
    "editorCursor.foreground": "#4CC4B4",
    "editorCursor.background": "#120C06",
    // Current line: grain surface, no border (border would be visually noisy).
    "editor.lineHighlightBackground": "#1E140E",
    "editor.lineHighlightBorder": "#00000000",
    // Line numbers: crater (muted) for inactive, mocha for active.
    "editorLineNumber.foreground": "#3C2A21",
    "editorLineNumber.activeForeground": "#8B7355",
    "editorLineNumber.dimmedForeground": "#2A1C13",

    // ── Selection & highlight ──────────────────────────────────────────────
    // Amber selection family — warm, consistent with the primary accent color.
    "editor.selectionBackground": "#E69A4C33",
    "editor.selectionHighlightBackground": "#E69A4C1A",
    "editor.selectionHighlightBorder": "#E69A4C44",
    "editor.inactiveSelectionBackground": "#E69A4C22",
    // Word highlight uses teal — "live data" — distinct from amber selection.
    "editor.wordHighlightBackground": "#4CC4B41A",
    "editor.wordHighlightBorder": "#4CC4B444",
    "editor.wordHighlightStrongBackground": "#4CC4B433",
    "editor.wordHighlightStrongBorder": "#4CC4B466",

    // ── Find & replace ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    "editor.findMatchBackground": "#E69A4C44",
    "editor.findMatchHighlightBackground": "#E69A4C22",

===== FILE: dark-roast-theme/platforms/warp/dark-roast-blue-mountain.yaml =====
# AUTO-GENERATED by scripts/build-variants.js — DO NOT EDIT.
# ============================================================================
# Dark Roast: Blue Mountain — Warp Terminal Theme
# Version: 5.1.0 Companion
#
# INSTALL
# -------
#   1. Copy this file to ~/.warp/themes/dark-roast-blue-mountain.yaml
#      (create ~/.warp/themes/ if it doesn't exist)
#   2. Open Warp → Settings → Appearance → Theme
#   3. Select "dark-roast-blue-mountain" from the dropdown
#
# PALETTE PHILOSOPHY
# ------------------
# All four Dark Roast terminal themes (Warp, Tabby, Terminal.app, iTerm2) share
# an identical ANSI-16 palette so that ls, git diff, vim syntax, tmux, and every
# other CLI tool produce exactly the same output regardless of which emulator
# you're running.
#
# The palette is grounded in the Dark Roast design system:
#   - Background/foreground pulled directly from DR tokens (void, crema)
#   - Cursor matches the editor cursor (teal — "kinetic, live data flow")
#   - Selection uses espresso (#052544) — warm but not glaring (v4: was `grain`)
#   - ANSI normals and brights use the five DR action colors + three
#     terminal-extension colors (sage, slate, mauve) that aren't in the core
#     UI token set but sit squarely within the warm espresso aesthetic
#
# FULL COLOR REFERENCE
# --------------------
# Chrome:
#   background    #000b1d   void      — warm-dark deepest layer
#   foreground    #e5ecf3   crema     — primary text (16.54:1 contrast on void)
#   cursor        #00b5b5   teal      — kinetic, matches editor caret
#   cursor text   #000b1d   void      — inverted on cursor block
#   selection bg  #052544   espresso  — warm polished surface (v4: was `grain`)
#   selection fg  #e5ecf3   crema     — full brightness on selection
#
# ANSI Normal (indices 0–7):
#   0 black       #001228   obsidian  — dark but not void; provides depth in dark bg
#   1 red         #f86572   scarlet   — error / critical
#   2 green       #60a563   sage      — warm fern green (terminal extension)
#   3 yellow      #ef912d   amber     — warning / accent / CTA
#   4 blue        #49accf   slate     — dusty steel blue (terminal extension)
#   5 magenta     #b181e5   mauve     — dried lavender (terminal extension)
#   6 cyan        #00b5b5   teal      — live data flow / resolved
#   7 white       #c3cfdc   bone      — reduced-contrast light text
#
# ANSI Bright (indices 8–15):
#   8  bright black    #8797a9   crater-deep   — comment gray / muted metadata (v4: was `crater`)
#   9  bright red      #f55e6c   scarlet-lt    — scarlet companion-bright
#  10  bright green    #6dba70   sage-lt       — sage companion-bright
#  11  bright yellow   #ebaa1f   gold          — success / stable severity
#  12  bright blue     #49c1ea   slate-lt      — slate companion-bright
#  13  bright magenta  #bd87f6   mauve-lt      — mauve companion-bright
#  14  bright cyan     #00caca   teal-lt       — teal brightened (noticeably lighter
#                                               than normal teal; brights should be
#                                               brighter, not identical)
#  15  bright white    #e5ecf3   crema         — full brightness
# ============================================================================

# ── Warp chrome ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
accent:     "#ef912d"   # amber — selection highlights and Warp UI accent ring
background: "#000b1d"   # void — warm-dark deepest layer
foreground: "#e5ecf3"   # crema — primary text, 16.54:1 contrast vs void
cursor:     "#00b5b5"   # teal — kinetic live-data cursor, matches editor caret
details:    darker      # Warp lightens or darkens chrome decoration; "darker"
                        # keeps tab bar and sidebar darker than the background,
                        # which is correct for a warm-dark bg

# ── ANSI-16 terminal colors ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
terminal_colors:
  normal:
    black:   "#001228"  # ANSI 0 — obsidian (elevated floor, not as deep as void)
    red:     "#f86572"  # ANSI 1 — scarlet (error / critical severity)
    green:   "#60a563"  # ANSI 2 — sage (warm fern, used by git diff +lines, ls dirs)
    yellow:  "#ef912d"  # ANSI 3 — amber (warning / accent; matches DR primary CTA)
    blue:    "#49accf"  # ANSI 4 — slate (dusty steel; git diff header, less prompt)
    magenta: "#b181e5"  # ANSI 5 — mauve (dried lavender; grep matches, vim special)
    cyan:    "#00b5b5"  # ANSI 6 — teal (live data; matches cursor + DR teal token)
    white:   "#c3cfdc"  # ANSI 7 — bone (reduced-contrast; comment-level brightness)

  bright:
    black:   "#8797a9"  # ANSI 8  — crater-deep (comment gray; git log graph, tmux inactive)
    red:     "#f55e6c"  # ANSI 9  — scarlet companion-bright (diff removed, error paths)
    green:   "#6dba70"  # ANSI 10 — sage companion-bright (diff added, success paths)
    yellow:  "#ebaa1f"  # ANSI 11 — gold (success / stable; DR gold token, git branch)
    blue:    "#49c1ea"  # ANSI 12 — slate companion-bright (links, prompt path segments)
    magenta: "#bd87f6"  # ANSI 13 — mauve companion-bright (vim visual, special tokens)
    cyan:    "#00caca"  # ANSI 14 — teal lightened (brighter than normal teal #00b5b5;
                        #            satisfies "bright should look brighter" convention)
    white:   "#e5ecf3"  # ANSI 15 — crema (full brightness; bold text, headings)

#
# PALETTE PHILOSOPHY
# ------------------
# All four Dark Roast terminal themes (Warp, Tabby, Terminal.app, iTerm2) share
# an identical ANSI-16 palette so that ls, git diff, vim syntax, tmux, and every
# other CLI tool produce exactly the same output regardless of which emulator
# you're running.
#
# The palette is grounded in the Dark Roast design system:
#   - Background/foreground pulled directly from DR tokens (void, crema)
#   - Cursor matches the editor cursor (teal — "kinetic, live data flow")
#   - Selection uses espresso (#3B2A20) — warm but not glaring (v4: was `grain`)
#   - ANSI normals and brights use the five DR action colors + three
#     terminal-extension colors (sage, slate, mauve) that aren't in the core
#     UI token set but sit squarely within the warm espresso aesthetic
#
# FULL COLOR REFERENCE
# --------------------
# Chrome:
#   background    #241810   void      — warm-dark deepest layer
#   foreground    #FFF8F0   crema     — primary text (16.43:1 contrast on void)
#   cursor        #2CB9AA   teal      — kinetic, matches editor caret
#   cursor text   #241810   void      — inverted on cursor block
#   selection bg  #3B2A20   espresso  — warm polished surface (v4: was `grain`)
#   selection fg  #FFF8F0   crema     — full brightness on selection
#
# ANSI Normal (indices 0–7):
#   0 black       #2B1D14   obsidian  — dark but not void; provides depth in dark bg
#   1 red         #FE8175   scarlet   — error / critical
#   2 green       #79B56C   sage      — warm fern green (terminal extension)
#   3 yellow      #E9922E   amber     — warning / accent / CTA
#   4 blue        #6AACE2   slate     — dusty steel blue (terminal extension)
#   5 magenta     #D28DE2   mauve     — dried lavender (terminal extension)
#   6 cyan        #2CB9AA   teal      — live data flow / resolved
#   7 white       #E9DCCF   bone      — reduced-contrast light text
#
# ANSI Bright (indices 8–15):
#   8  bright black    #BCA18A   crater-deep   — comment gray / muted metadata (v4: was `crater`)
#   9  bright red      #FF9286   scarlet-lt    — scarlet companion-bright
#  10  bright green    #98D083   sage-lt       — sage companion-bright
#  11  bright yellow   #D0A200   gold          — success / stable severity
#  12  bright blue     #68C7F4   slate-lt      — slate companion-bright
#  13  bright magenta  #E792DF   mauve-lt      — mauve companion-bright
#  14  bright cyan     #72D8CA   teal-lt       — teal brightened (noticeably lighter
#                                               than normal teal; brights should be
#                                               brighter, not identical)
#  15  bright white    #FFF8F0   crema         — full brightness
# ============================================================================

# ── Warp chrome ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
accent:     "#E9922E"   # amber — selection highlights and Warp UI accent ring
background: "#241810"   # void — warm-dark deepest layer
foreground: "#FFF8F0"   # crema — primary text, 16.43:1 contrast vs void
cursor:     "#2CB9AA"   # teal — kinetic live-data cursor, matches editor caret
details:    darker      # Warp lightens or darkens chrome decoration; "darker"
                        # keeps tab bar and sidebar darker than the background,
                        # which is correct for a warm-dark bg

# ── ANSI-16 terminal colors ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
terminal_colors:
  normal:

    red:     "#FF9286"  # ANSI 9  — scarlet companion-bright (diff removed, error paths)
    green:   "#98D083"  # ANSI 10 — sage companion-bright (diff added, success paths)
    yellow:  "#D0A200"  # ANSI 11 — gold (success / stable; DR gold token, git branch)
    blue:    "#68C7F4"  # ANSI 12 — slate companion-bright (links, prompt path segments)

#   3 yellow      #E69A4C   amber     — warning / accent / CTA
#   4 blue        #6E8FAD   slate     — dusty steel blue (terminal extension)
#   5 magenta     #AD7FA8   mauve     — dried lavender (terminal extension)
#   6 cyan        #4CC4B4   teal      — live data flow / resolved
#   7 white       #EBE1D7   bone      — reduced-contrast light text
#
# ANSI Bright (indices 8–15):
#   8  bright black    #3C2A21   crater-deep   — comment gray / muted metadata (v4: was `crater`)
#   9  bright red      #D46868   scarlet-lt    — scarlet lightened (~20%)
#  10  bright green    #A3C484   sage-lt       — sage lightened (~20%)
#  11  bright yellow   #DAA520   gold          — success / stable severity
#  12  bright blue     #8AABC4   slate-lt      — slate lightened (~20%)
#  13  bright magenta  #C49BC0   mauve-lt      — mauve lightened (~20%)
#  14  bright cyan     #6DD4C8   teal-lt       — teal brightened (noticeably lighter
#                                               than normal teal; brights should be
#                                               brighter, not identical)
#  15  bright white    #FFF7EE   crema         — full brightness
# ============================================================================

# ── Warp chrome ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
accent:     "#E69A4C"   # amber — selection highlights and Warp UI accent ring
background: "#120C06"   # void — OLED-safe deepest layer (1.6ms pixel wake)
foreground: "#FFF7EE"   # crema — primary text, 18.31:1 contrast vs void
cursor:     "#4CC4B4"   # teal — kinetic live-data cursor, matches editor caret
details:    darker      # Warp lightens or darkens chrome decoration; "darker"
                        # keeps tab bar and sidebar darker than the background,
                        # which is correct for a near-black bg

# ── ANSI-16 terminal colors ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
terminal_colors:
  normal:
    black:   "#160E08"  # ANSI 0 — obsidian (elevated floor, not as deep as void)
    red:     "#C44C4C"  # ANSI 1 — scarlet (error / critical severity)
    green:   "#8AAC6B"  # ANSI 2 — sage (warm fern, used by git diff +lines, ls dirs)
    yellow:  "#E69A4C"  # ANSI 3 — amber (warning / accent; matches DR primary CTA)
    blue:    "#6E8FAD"  # ANSI 4 — slate (dusty steel; git diff header, less prompt)
    magenta: "#AD7FA8"  # ANSI 5 — mauve (dried lavender; grep matches, vim special)
    cyan:    "#4CC4B4"  # ANSI 6 — teal (live data; matches cursor + DR teal token)
    white:   "#EBE1D7"  # ANSI 7 — bone (reduced-contrast; comment-level brightness)

  bright:
    black:   "#3C2A21"  # ANSI 8  — crater-deep (comment gray; git log graph, tmux inactive)
    red:     "#D46868"  # ANSI 9  — scarlet lightened ~20% (diff removed, error paths)
    green:   "#A3C484"  # ANSI 10 — sage lightened ~20% (diff added, success paths)
    yellow:  "#DAA520"  # ANSI 11 — gold (success / stable; DR gold token, git branch)
    blue:    "#8AABC4"  # ANSI 12 — slate lightened ~20% (links, prompt path segments)
    magenta: "#C49BC0"  # ANSI 13 — mauve lightened ~20% (vim visual, special tokens)
    cyan:    "#6DD4C8"  # ANSI 14 — teal lightened (brighter than normal teal #4CC4B4;
                        #            satisfies "bright should look brighter" convention)
    white:   "#FFF7EE"  # ANSI 15 — crema (full brightness; bold text, headings)

  DESIGN PHILOSOPHY — THE KILLER FEATURE:

  Xcode uniquely separates user-defined from SDK/system identifiers.
  This theme exploits that distinction as its primary visual grammar:

    WARM PALETTE  →  YOUR code
      gold   #DAA520  your classes, structs, enums, type aliases
      teal   #4CC4B4  your functions and methods
      amber  #E69A4C  your attributes (@State, @objc), your macros
      amber-hot #D2691E  numeric literals, your constants, system constants

    COOL SLATE  →  Apple's SDK
      slate  #6E8FAD  UIViewController, Int, String, system funcs, etc.

    STRUCTURAL MAUVE  →  Language itself
      mauve  #AD7FA8  keywords (if/let/func/class), preprocessor (#import),
                      system variables (self, super) — language-reserved

      sage   #8AAC6B  string and character literals (organic, universal)
      mocha  #8B7355  comments (must recede completely)
      bone   #EBE1D7  doc comment keywords (scannable above mocha base)
      crema  #FFF7EE  plain text, user variables (most common token)

  After 30 minutes of coding your eyes internalize: warm = mine, cool =
  Apple's. This is the fastest way to read Swift/ObjC in a dark editor.
